key_insight: Even when every delegated quantum round is blinded, the total round count can reveal private information through the optimizer’s stopping time.
engineering_relevance: Secure delegated variational quantum algorithms need stopping-time protections beyond per-round encryption, with fixed public budgets eliminating this channel at a utility cost.
method: Prove that sequence-level distinguishing advantage equals the total-variation distance between stopping-time distributions under fresh, one-time-padded rounds.
Bound adaptive-stop soundness error by δ·E[T], assuming conditional per-round soundness.
Evaluate simulated delegated eigensolvers and compare fixed-budget, padding, and private-stopping defenses.
evidence_signal: Across 14 simulated configurations, leakage was significant in 12 and ranged from 0.14 to 1.68 bits; an early-iteration convergence metric predicted noiseless stopping within 1.7 iterations versus 10.3 for a constant predictor.
watch_item: The sole-channel result assumes fresh per-round randomness and one-time-padded transcripts; defenses can trade leakage reduction for extra rounds or premature stopping.
paper_title: Stopping-Time Leakage in Blind Quantum Delegation
